item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really like the idea of the Foundation having a - pardon the irresistible pun - cunning linguist on staff and I loved the original trick Mellows played on the prisoner with the water, but c'mon. It's lines like the following that are killing this:

"Dr Lee: Right you bastard. You just made me look like a [EXPLETIVE] in front of the stuck-up Limey. He carries that damn umbrella with him everywhere you know, even midsummer."

This isn't about Mr. Mellows. To be specific, this shouldn't be about Mr. Mellows. This is an interview log for SCP-418 and should be about SCP-418. Gratuitous lines about Mr. Mellows like that make it obvious that this entire thing is an artifice to flesh out a Foundation character and that is the opposite of what anything on the main list should be doing.

item.content:encoded:
I like how they arrive at the conclusion, but the format sounds more like a story and less like an interview log. What you might do is have the two go off-camera for a second and speak quietly, then return and make their accusations.

Also, the bit where he orders the 'water D' bit is still confusing. I've never heard it defined elsewhere, so you might want to find a way to slip in a note at the beginning like 'Dr. __ notes that if subject is not cooperative, a serving of water D with _ drug is to be requested'.

Hilarious smackdown.

I've never heard an American say 'pillock'. It sounds strange to have a non-Brit insult Mellows ("limey") and then use what sounds like a Britishism. Possible American words to substitute include 'dope' or 'moron'.

Also, Mellows specifically says 'nothing special in the water'; he never mentions anything suspicious about the water.
